botanical_name: Mentha spp. (commonly Mentha arvensis, Mentha spicata, Mentha x piperita)
description: A creeping, strongly aromatic perennial herb with square stems, opposite toothed leaves and whorled spikes of small pale purple or white flowers. It spreads quickly by runners (stolons).
cultural_significance: Pudina is part of everyday Indian cooking, in chutneys, raita, chaas and beverages, and is valued as a cooling digestive. Mentha arvensis is a major source of menthol in India. It is not a Vedic-era plant by name; it is prominent in later texts and household practice.
habitat: Moist, fertile, partially shaded soils along streams, ditches and irrigated fields; widely grown in kitchen gardens and as a field crop.

uses.title: Digestive support
uses.detail: Described as Deepana-Pachana (appetiser and digestive); leaf juice, chutney or buttermilk with mint is traditionally used for indigestion, bloating and loss of appetite.

uses.title: Nausea and vomiting
uses.detail: Fresh leaf juice with a little honey or lemon is a traditional household remedy for nausea.

uses.title: Cold, cough and headache
uses.detail: Inhaling steam with mint leaves or applying diluted mint oil is traditionally used to relieve blocked nose and tension headache.

uses.title: Oral freshness
uses.detail: Chewing leaves or gargling with a leaf infusion is a common practice for bad breath.

uses.title: Irritable bowel research
uses.detail: Enteric-coated peppermint oil has been studied for relief of irritable bowel symptoms; evidence is moderate and applies to the oil, not to raw leaves.

preparations.name: Swarasa (fresh leaf juice)
preparations.method: Crush fresh leaves and press out the juice; taken with honey or lemon.
preparations.note: Small quantities; used for nausea and indigestion.

preparations.name: Pudina chutney
preparations.method: Grind fresh leaves with coriander, green chilli, salt and lemon juice.

preparations.name: Mint tea (hot infusion)
preparations.method: Steep fresh or dried leaves in hot water for 5-7 minutes.

preparations.name: Pudina arka (distillate)
preparations.method: Steam distillation of the leaves gives an aromatic water traditionally used for stomach upset.

precautions: Menthol-rich oil should not be applied to or near the face of infants and young children because it can cause breathing problems. Peppermint can aggravate acid reflux or heartburn in some people and may interact with medicines processed by the liver. Pure mint oil is toxic if swallowed in quantity and should be diluted for external use. Large medicinal amounts should be avoided in pregnancy.

cultivation.climate: Temperate to subtropical; grows best in cool, moist conditions
cultivation.propagation: Runners or stem cuttings; division of clumps
cultivation.harvest: Cut stems before flowering; multiple harvests a year

fun_fact: India is among the world's leading producers of menthol mint (Mentha arvensis), grown across the Gangetic plains of Uttar Pradesh.
